activities.title: Playdough and pinch warm-up
parentPrompts: Roll playdough into a snake, then a ball, then pinch it with just the thumb and pointer finger. Tell your child strong writing hands start with strong fingers.
Clip clothespins onto the edge of a paper plate, one at a time, using only the thumb and pointer finger.
Ask: "Which was harder, pinching or rolling?" Let them decide and show you the harder one again.
Look for: a thumb-and-pointer pinch (not a whole-fist squeeze). If it is hard, repeat this warm-up for a few days before moving on.

activities.title: Draw straight lines
materials: a tray of salt or dry sand (optional)
parentPrompts: Draw a standing line (top to bottom) and a sleeping line (left to right). Say each name as you draw it.
Have your child draw 5 standing lines in a row, then 5 sleeping lines. Use a finger in a salt tray first if paper feels hard.
Ask: "Can you make a standing line from the top of the page to the bottom?" Cheer for any try.
Look for: lines that start at the top and move down, and start at the left and move right. Gently show the starting point if they begin elsewhere.

activities.title: Big and small circles
parentPrompts: Draw a big circle in the air with your whole arm, then a smaller one with just your hand.
On paper, draw a circle together. Then let your child try several, big and small.
Add curves: draw a rainbow arch and a smile curve. Ask: "Which one looks like a ball? Which one looks like a smile?"
Look for: a closed circle drawn in one smooth motion. Tracing around a plate counts too.

activities.title: Slanting lines and crosses
parentPrompts: Draw a slanting line going down to the right, then one going down to the left. Make an X by crossing them.
Ask your child to make 3 big X marks, like marking treasure on a map.
Make an X with two playdough sticks or two pencils laid across each other.
Ask: "Where do the two lines cross?" Look for: they cross in the middle and both lines are about the same length.

subject: literacy
title: The first letter of my name

activities.title: Write the first letter of my name
parentPrompts: Write your child's first name with a capital first letter and lowercase for the rest, using the same letter shapes they will see in books.
Point to the first letter. Say: "This big letter is the start of your name." Trace it together with a finger.
Have them copy just that first letter 3 times on paper. You can help by writing a light dot where each letter starts.
Ask: "Which letter is this? What name does it start?" Look for: letter formed from the top, in the right direction. Praise effort, not neatness.

activities.title: Count one at a time
materials: 10 small things like blocks, buttons or large pasta
parentPrompts: Line up 5 things. Say: "We touch each one and say one number." Count together, touching each item once.
Ask: "How many are there?" Let them answer with the last number. Repeat with 3, 4 and 6 things.
Now let them do the counting while you watch. Slide each item aside as it is counted so none is missed or counted twice.
Look for: one touch per item and a steady voice. Safety: small items are a choking hazard for babies and toddlers, so keep them away from younger siblings and out of mouths.

subject: math
title: The last number tells how many

activities.title: Same amount, different arrangement
parentPrompts: Count 6 things in a line. Ask: "How many?" Then spread them out in a circle and ask again before counting.
Many children count again from one. Count together and show that the last number said is the amount, still 6.
Try 4 things, then 7. Each time, change the arrangement and ask: "Is it still the same number?"

Look for: your child says the last number counted as the answer, and starts to trust that it stays the same. Safety: small items are a choking hazard for babies and toddlers, so keep them away from younger siblings and out of mouths.

activities.title: Match numerals to groups
parentPrompts: Write the numerals 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 each on its own card. Name each one and trace it with a finger.
Place the cards in a row. Have your child put that many things under each card.
Mix the cards, hold one up and ask: "Show me this many." Then turn it around: you show some things, they pick the card.

Look for: correct number of items under each card and correct naming of 1 to 5. Safety: small items are a choking hazard for babies and toddlers, so keep them away from younger siblings and out of mouths.

activities.title: Cups and numerals 6 to 10
materials: 30 small things like dry pasta or buttons
parentPrompts: Write 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 on the bottom of five cups. Name each numeral.
Ask your child to put that many things in each cup, counting out loud and touching each one.
Pour one cup out and count again to check. Ask: "Which cup has the most? How do you know?"

Look for: they match the numeral to the right amount, counting each one carefully. Safety: small items are a choking hazard for babies and toddlers, so keep them away from younger siblings and out of mouths.

activities.title: Build a tower, one more at a time
parentPrompts: Build a tower of 3 blocks. Ask: "What if I add one more? How many now?" Count to check.
Keep adding one block at a time. Each time say: "One more makes..." and let them finish.
Try it from other numbers: start with 5 blocks and ask what one more is. Then 8.
Look for: they can say the next number without counting from one. If not, recount together; this skill grows with practice.

activities.title: Front cover, back cover and title page
parentPrompts: Hold the book and ask: "Where is the front? Where is the back?" Point to the front cover and back cover together.
Show the title page, the page inside that repeats the title. Say: "The title is the name of the book."
Read the book together with expression. Stop at the end and say: "The back cover is last."
Ask: "Can you find the front cover on another book?" Look for: they can point to the front cover, back cover and title page.

activities.title: Who wrote it, who drew it?
materials: a picture book with author and illustrator named on the cover
parentPrompts: Show the cover. Say: "The author writes the words. The illustrator draws the pictures." Point to each name.
Read the story. Cover the words on one page and say: "Who made these pictures?" Then cover the pictures and ask: "Who wrote these words?"
Ask: "If you made a book, would you be the author, the illustrator or both?"
Look for: your child can tell the author from the illustrator with prompting.

activities.title: Follow the words with a finger
materials: a picture book with big print
a craft stick as a pointer
parentPrompts: Read a page and use the stick to point to each word as you say it. Move left to right, then drop down to the next line.
Say: "Words go this way," and show the sweep. Then let your child be the pointer while you read.
Ask: "Where do I start reading on this page? Where do I go next?" Turn the pages together and ask which side to read first.
Look for: they can show where reading starts and the direction it moves.

activities.title: Count the words
parentPrompts: Read one short sentence from the book and point to each word. Say: "Spaces show where one word stops."
Put one block down for every word you hear and see. Count them: "The cat sat. How many words?"
Let your child choose a sentence and do the same. Cover a word and ask which one is missing.
Look for: they can point to separate words and notice spaces between them.

activities.title: Letters and words in a book
parentPrompts: Open to a page and say: "Letters sit together to make words. Words say what we say out loud." Point to a short word and say it.
Ask your child to find a letter they know on the page. Then find a word that starts with it.
Write a short word like 'cat' on a card. Say it, then point to each letter.
Look for: they know letters are the marks and words are what the letters spell, and can point to a letter and a word.

activities.title: Plant bean seeds and wonder
materials: 6 dry beans such as lima or pinto (do not eat raw dry beans)
a sunny window and a dark closet
parentPrompts: Plant 2 beans in each of 3 cups about 2 centimeters deep. Wash hands afterward. Safety: dry beans are small objects and should not be eaten raw or put in mouths.
Cup A: window light and water. Cup B: window light, no water. Cup C: dark closet, water. Say: "We will watch and find out what plants need."
Ask: "What do you think will happen in each cup?" Draw their guesses on paper.
Water A and C each day or two (just damp, not soaked). Look for: they can make a guess and say what is different about each cup. Keep checking in the next lessons.

activities.title: Watch an animal
materials: a pet, a bird feeder or a window with a view of birds or insects
parentPrompts: Watch an animal for a few minutes. Look from a distance and do not touch wild animals. Wash hands if you touch a pet.
Ask: "What is the animal doing? What does it eat? Where does it get water? Where does it rest or hide?"
Say: "Animals need food, water, air and a safe place to live." Draw the animal and one of its needs.
Look for: they can name at least two things the animal needs. If no animal is nearby, use pictures from a book.

activities.title: Needs and wants
parentPrompts: Say: "People are animals too. We need food, water, air, a safe place to live and sleep."
Fold a paper in half. Draw or find pictures of things we need on one side and things we like but could do without (like a favorite toy) on the other.
Ask: "What does our family do to get food and water?" Talk about how we take care of ourselves.
Look for: they can say at least two needs. Be gentle with the wants; this is about noticing, not judging.

activities.title: Why we have rules
parentPrompts: Ask: "What are some rules at our home?" (for example, walk inside, wash hands, be kind). Listen without judging.
Say: "Rules help keep us safe and help everyone get a turn."
Draw one rule and one reason for it. Write the rule for them.
Look for: they can say a rule and what it helps with. Families have different rules; that is fine.

activities.title: Places we go
materials: a walk in your neighborhood or photos
parentPrompts: Say: "A community is a group of people who live or work near each other." Ask: "Where do we go in our community?" (store, library, park, school or others).
Take a short walk or look at pictures. Name each place and what people do there.
Draw a favorite place.
Look for: they name 2 or 3 places and what we do there. All kinds of communities are good: a city, a town or farmland.

activities.title: Clap and tap names
parentPrompts: Clap the parts of your child's name. Then clap family names.
Tap the beat on a pot with a spoon. Make a pattern: loud, soft, loud, soft.
Take turns copying each other's pattern.
Look for: they can copy a simple rhythm. Keep the volume friendly.

activities.title: Line collage
parentPrompts: Draw different kinds of lines: straight, wavy, zigzag, curly.
Glue pieces of yarn onto the page to make lines.
Ask: "What does this line make you think of?"
Look for: they use more than one kind of line. Talk about what they made.

activities.title: Draw myself
parentPrompts: Look in the mirror together. Say what you see: hair, eyes, nose, mouth.
Draw their face large on the page. Add details.
Ask: "What color are your eyes? What shape is your face?"
Look for: they include a few features. Everyone's face and skin tone is different; celebrate that.

activities.title: Paint with found colors
parentPrompts: Find things around the house of one color, like red or blue.
Paint a picture using only that color, in light and dark versions by adding water or a little white.
Ask: "What did you notice about the color?"
Look for: they enjoy the paint and name the colors. Clean up together.

activities.title: Sing and count
parentPrompts: Sing a counting rhyme or song you know, such as 'One, Two, Buckle My Shoe' or another traditional rhyme.
Add motions: hold up fingers for each number.
Make up a silly new verse with your own numbers.
Look for: they can sing in order and match motions.
